intro: Big Bad Brain Wrestling: the physics of fake pain and the economy of real ego.
outro: It's still real to me, dammit!

lines.triplet: The Babyface uses high-flying moves because audiences cheer for that? A slave to approval.
The Heel: bear hugs and eye pokes. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener? You don't ask for it, which makes them want you more.
The Jobber exists to make the other guy look good. Only control: who defeats you.
The Immovable Object: slow, but strong enough to hurl you like a ragdoll.
The Aerial Ace: agile and fast. If you stand still, you die.

lines.pre: Never tell a gorilla that, or you get
lines.triplet: The Powerhouse Botch, leaping off the top rope: a tragedy waiting to happen.
The Little Giant: smaller wrestlers, surprising strength.
The Master Seller: reel back, limp to the ring, make them believe.
The No-Sell Monster: sit right back up just to prove how dangerous you are.
The Oversell Clown, reacting to an attack far beyond reality. See: Michaels and Hogan.
The Thigh Slap: the move didn't hurt, but it sounds like it did. An audio lie.
The Stomp Punch: stomping on the mat when punching. Kinetic misdirection.
The Chop Fest: nothing but chop, until one quits. A test of endurance.
The Sacred Mask is the single biggest identifier? Never remove it.
The Rudo Ripper attempts to maim the mask: instant disqualification, but you win the feud.
The Juice Lover: you can't hurt me if I hurt me first.
The Snake Bag: the bag has a live snake. Terrify them before the match starts.
The Lazy Genius does: hands in pockets, it looks like a chore. The apathy makes them furious.

lines.pre: Furious people are easy prey for
lines.triplet: The Exotic, harming the opponent's dignity rather than their body.
The Hot Tag: fresh partner for payback, the explosive release of tension.
The Victim, the Ricky Morton role: isolated and picked apart. You are the bait.
The Wolfpack: brawler, flyer, powerhouse. Triple attack on an isolated target.
The Savant Manager: you know the moves better than they do.
The Pop Hunter: if they want a heel, give them a heel. If they want a clown, honk your nose.
The Empty Arena, pausing for a pop that never comes: silence amplifies the sound of impacts.
The Green Screen Crowd: pipe in noise, audio sweetening on a lie.

lines.pre: And the guy in the front row?
lines.triplet: The Plant: I'm just a fan! Gambling on the outcome while part of the show.

lines.pre: There's always one who won't play along:
lines.triplet: The Shooter forces opponent to sell. If they refuse, real damage.
The Sandbag, refusing to cooperate. Dead weight. Extremely unprofessional.

lines.pre: Guess what the crowd loves most?
lines.triplet: The Real Injury, unplanned. The crowd goes nuts because it's real.
The Trash Talker, shouting at Michael Cole: hilarious and entertaining abuse.
The Finger Poke was a test of strength? No, a test of gullibility.

lines.pre: Fall for it, and here comes
lines.triplet: The Finisher, the Leg Drop: the most important moment. If this hits, go home.
The False Finish, the art of the near-fall. Crowd excitement doubles.
The Time Limit Draw: no winner, both players keep their dignity.
The Booker decides the winner before the game starts: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.
The Spot Caller: a basic outline, filled in with sweat.
The Rehearsal: perfect, but lacks soul. Hogan and Warrior.
The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.
The Announcer's Table: shouting at Michael Cole while destroying his desk.
The Internet Smark, talking about psychology without ever taking a bump.
The Botched Spot, an incoherent collection of moves. It just looks messy.
The Kayfabe Police: keep the secrets secret, or get fired.

lines.pre: And when it all gets too much, there's
lines.triplet: The Retirement Match: rising, and falling. See you next season.
